unit.unitOverview:
Say the parts of the day.
Say the days of the week.
Say what you do every day.
Say when you do it.
unit.learningPath:
Listen to the lesson.
Words: times of day and the week.
Patterns: in the morning, and on Monday.
Listen to three short texts.
Tell your day. Record it.
Write about one day.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
functions: Say the parts of the day
Say the days of the week
Say what you do every day
Say when you do a thing
Ask another person about their day

visual.lectureScript:
This is Unit 15. One day, from start to end.
First, the parts of a day.
The morning. The afternoon.
The evening. The night.
Say them with me.
Now the small word that goes with them.
In the morning. In the afternoon.
In the evening. But at night.
Night is different. At night.
Say them with me. In the morning. At night.
Now the week. You know some already.
Monday. Friday. Saturday. Sunday.
Say them with me.
And the word for a day of the week: on.
On Monday. On Friday. On Sunday.
So: in the morning, but on Monday.
Now what you do.
I get up at six.
I wash. I walk to work.
I sleep at ten.
Say them with me. I get up. I wash. I walk. I sleep.
And the three words that hold a day together.
Every day. Today. Tomorrow.
I work every day. Today is Monday.
Tomorrow is Tuesday.
That is Unit 15. Go and tell your day.

readings.title: My Day
readings.genre: One person describing a normal day
readings.setting: A flat and a workplace, over one day
readings.passageScript:
I get up at six in the morning.
I wash and I eat bread.
I walk to work. It is ten minutes.
I start at seven.
I finish at four in the afternoon.
I walk home.
In the evening I study English.
I sleep at ten at night.
Every day is the same.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: In the morning, but at night
grammar.explanation:
Three parts of the day take in.
One takes at.
That one is night.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
in the morning
in the afternoon
in the evening

at night

I work in the morning.
I sleep at night.
grammar.workedExample:
You want to say you study after work.
1. That is the evening.
2. Evening takes in.
3. Say: I study in the evening.
4. Now say when you sleep.
5. Night takes at: I sleep at night.
grammar.commonMistake:
No: in the night.
Yes: at night.
It is the only one of the four that changes.
grammar.memoryTip: Three in, one at. Night is the at.
grammar.practice:
Write in or at.
1. ___ the morning
2. ___ night
3. ___ the evening
4. ___ the afternoon
5. I work ___ the morning.
6. I sleep ___ night.
grammar.answerKey:
1. in
2. at
3. in
4. in
5. in
6. at
Five or six right? Night is the one to remember.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: On Monday
grammar.explanation:
A day of the week takes on.
That is different from a part of the day.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
on Monday
on Friday
on Saturday
on Sunday

But: in the morning, at night

I work on Monday.
I work on Monday morning.
grammar.workedExample:
Your class is on the first day of the week.
1. Monday is a day of the week.
2. Days take on.
3. Say: The class is on Monday.
4. Add a part of the day: on Monday morning.
5. The on stays, and in is not needed.
grammar.commonMistake:
No: in Monday.
Yes: on Monday.
Days take on. Parts of the day take in.
grammar.memoryTip: Days take on. Parts of the day take in.
grammar.practice:
Write in, on or at.
1. ___ Monday
2. ___ the morning
3. ___ night
4. ___ Friday
5. ___ the evening
6. ___ Sunday
7. ___ the afternoon
8. ___ Saturday
grammar.answerKey:
1. on
2. in
3. at
4. on
5. in
6. on
7. in
8. on
Six or more right? You can say when a thing happens.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: What I do every day
grammar.explanation:
Say your day in order.
Four short lines is a whole routine.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
I get up at six.
I wash.
I walk to work.
I sleep at ten.

he, she, it → add s
She gets up at six.
He walks to work.
grammar.workedExample:
You want to tell somebody your day.
1. Start at the beginning: I get up at six.
2. Then the next thing: I wash.
3. Then work: I walk to work.
4. Then the end: I sleep at ten.
5. Four lines is enough for a whole day.
grammar.commonMistake:
No: She get up at six.
Yes: She gets up at six.
He, she and it add an s to the verb.
grammar.memoryTip: Put your day in order, from morning to night.
grammar.practice:
Write the verb with or without s.
1. I ___ (get up) at six.
2. She ___ (get up) at seven.
3. He ___ (walk) to work.
4. I ___ (sleep) at ten.
5. She ___ (wash) in the morning.
grammar.answerKey:
1. get up
2. gets up
3. walks
4. sleep
5. washes
Four or five right? Washes takes es, not just s.

grammar.reviewStatus: Script review and curriculum sign-off pending
grammar.title: Today and tomorrow
grammar.explanation:
Two words that hold your week together.
They need no in, on or at.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
Today is Monday.
Tomorrow is Tuesday.

I am busy today.
I will come tomorrow.

No word before them:
No: on today.   Yes: today.
grammar.workedExample:
You cannot come to work until the next day.
1. The next day is tomorrow.
2. No small word is needed.
3. Say: I will come tomorrow.
4. For this day: I am ill today.
5. Never say on today or in tomorrow.
grammar.commonMistake:
No: I will come on tomorrow.
Yes: I will come tomorrow.
grammar.memoryTip: Today and tomorrow take no small word.
grammar.practice:
Right or wrong?
1. I am busy today.
2. I will come on tomorrow.
3. Today is Monday.
4. In tomorrow I work.
5. See you tomorrow.
grammar.answerKey:
1. Right
2. Wrong — I will come tomorrow.
3. Right
4. Wrong — Tomorrow I work.
5. Right
Four or five right? Good.

I walk to work.

writing.promptAndInstructions:

Sunday is my day off.
On Sunday I rest.
writing.successCriteria:
Four lines.
At least three different days named.
On before every day of the week.
Each line ends with a full stop.
writing.extension: Add a line saying which day you like best.
